results.title: Social Media Copyright and Fair Use Rules to Know | Ignite Social Media
results.content: Open law book on a desk — social media copyright and fair use. It’s so easy to grab music, sounds or images on social media and reuse them. As you use social media platforms to build your brand, you shouldn’t overlook the legal consequences that might arise. ## **Fair Use in the Social Media Age**. It’s a no-brainer that you shouldn’t use other people’s intellectual work without a fair use exemption or the owners’ permission. The fair use doctrine is part of the Copyright Act. It’s meant to limit the scope of copyright using an equitable rule of reason. However, if you’re using the content for commercial purposes, it falls outside the realm of fair use. ***TL/DR #1: If you’re using content for commercial purposes, you lose your fair use exemption.***. Using other people’s content can get you sued, more so if you’re a brand. The best way to avoid copyright lawsuits is by asking for permission to use the original creator’s work.

results.title: Copyright Online and Fair Use in Social Media
results.content: # Copyright Online and Fair Use in Social Media. Whether you’re sharing images on social media or using visuals in your marketing materials, it's essential to know how to protect your business and respect the rights of content creators. ## Understanding Social Media Copyright Risks. This is especially true for social media, where the boundaries of copyright and fair use are still being defined. Familiarizing yourself with copyright principles and specific platform guidelines can help protect your business from potential legal issues. ## What Is Copyright? ## Copyright Infringement and Fair Use. Courts consider several factors when determining if a use falls under fair use, including:. However, reposting an entire copyrighted song on social media without permission, even for non-commercial purposes, is typically deemed copyright infringement. To avoid copyright issues altogether, it’s wise to use royalty-free images and videos that are licensed for commercial use. While it’s unlikely that you’ll face legal action for using a meme like “Damn, Daniel” in a social media post, memes that feature copyrighted characters (like Futurama’s Fry or Boromir from "Lord of the Rings") could potentially lead to legal issues. These characters belong to specific brands or companies, and unauthorized use could be considered copyright infringement. Using memes in social media advertising is the riskiest area when it comes to copyright. Advertising is not protected by fair use, meaning any direct promotion of your brand using copyrighted memes can lead to legal consequences. Given the ambiguity surrounding fair use and copyright on social media, a good rule of thumb is to assume that all images and videos found online are protected by copyright unless explicitly stated otherwise by the owner. Ultimately, it is up to the content creator to enforce their copyright if their work is used without permission. As social media trends continue to evolve, so too will copyright laws and content-sharing practices. ## Copyright Registration: Protecting Your Creative Work. While understanding how to avoid infringing on others’ copyrights is important, it’s also worth considering protecting your own work. Registration is not required to own a copyright but offers additional protections and can be a valuable step in safeguarding your creative work.

Title: Webinar on Legal aspects of collecting and sharing social media data (copyright) - CLARIN Switzerland
# Webinar on Legal aspects of collecting and sharing social media data (copyright). The November webinar will be on **Legal aspects of collecting and sharing social media data (copyright)** and is organised within the CLARIN-CH Working Group **Management of Sensitive and Personal data, Ethical and Legal issues for linguistic data**. The recording and the slides of the webinar can be accessed here:. **Join us for a webinar on the legal challenges surrounding the use of social media data for language research purposes**, covering essential topics such as copyright and text-and-data mining (TDM) exceptions, the importance of terms of service, and data protection laws. We will also delve into the new regulatory framework under the Digital Services Act, exploring its implications for data use across various platforms. Whatever your research focus, if you use social media data, this session will provide valuable guidance on navigating the complex legal landscape. **Paweł Kamocki** is a researcher at the Leibniz-Institut für Deutsche Sprache and Chair of the CLARIN Legal and Ethical Issues Committee. He holds a Doctor of Law (Dr. iur.) degree (Münster, Paris), as well as a Master’s degree in linguistics (Warsaw), and graduated from the Paris Barrister Training School. His scientific interests are centered around legal issues affecting data-intensive science, especially in the field of linguistics and Digital Humanities; he published a number of peer-reviewed articles and book chapters on these questions. He also co-chaired the Working group on Data Access and Re-Use Policies and helped develop such Legal Tech tools as the Public License Selector and the DARIAH ELDAH Consent Form Wizard. This webinar is part of a series of webinars, which are taking place monthly during the spring and autumn semester 2024. **Discover the list of webinars here.**. ## Post navigation. ###### Previous Post.
